content.value_statement: Compound libraries need consistent triage before expensive review. This skill helps apply medicinal chemistry rules, structural alerts, and batch reports.
actual_capabilities: Apply Lipinski, Veber, CNS, leadlike, REOS, and related rule filters.
Flag PAINS patterns, common structural alerts, NIBR filters, and Lilly demerits.
Detect selected chemical groups such as hinge binders, phosphate binders, and reactive groups.
Calculate molecular complexity metrics including Bertz, Whitlock, and Barone scores.
Run batch filtering on CSV, TSV, SDF, and SMILES text files with summary output.
Build property constraints for molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bonds, and rotatable bonds.
limitations: Requires the medchem Python package and related chemistry dependencies.
Rules are screening guides and cannot predict clinical success.
Output quality depends on valid molecule structures and correct SMILES columns.
Does not replace expert medicinal chemistry or toxicology review.

use_cases.title: Triage a compound library
use_cases.description: Apply common drug-likeness rules and structural alerts before selecting molecules for review.

use_cases.title: Build a batch screening workflow
use_cases.description: Combine rules, alerts, complexity limits, and output reports for repeatable library filtering.

use_cases.title: Prepare chemistry data for decisions
use_cases.description: Summarize pass rates, failed criteria, and problematic motifs for project discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Check core drug-likeness
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner screening of a small compound set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the medchem skill to review my compound library. Apply Lipinski and Veber rules, then summarize pass rates and key concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Screen structural alerts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of a SMILES list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter this SMILES set for PAINS, common alerts, and NIBR issues. Return a short table of rejected molecules and reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Design lead optimization filters
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow planning for a lead series.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a medchem workflow for lead optimization. Combine leadlike strict rules, Lilly demerits, complexity under 400, and target-specific notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a filtering workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before a large library run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my medchem filtering script for reproducibility, inputs, outputs, and rule choices. Suggest changes for a large library run.

output_examples.input: A CSV with aspirin-like analogs and a request for Lipinski and Veber screening.
output_examples.output: A concise report with molecule counts, pass rates, failed rule categories, and recommended compounds for follow-up.

output_examples.input: A SMILES list for a kinase project with requested hinge binder and reactive group checks.
output_examples.output: A grouped summary of detected motifs, rejected reactive compounds, and compounds that need manual review.

output_examples.input: A lead series filtered with NIBR, Lilly demerits, and complexity limits.
output_examples.output: A ranked shortlist with filter status, likely liabilities, and clear notes for chemistry review.

best_practices: Choose rules that match the project stage and target biology.
Keep the original molecule identifiers with every filtered result.
Review rejected compounds manually before removing important chemotypes.
anti_patterns: Using every filter at once without a project rationale.
Treating pass or fail results as final safety or efficacy decisions.
Filtering libraries without recording thresholds, versions, and input files.

faq.question: Does this skill discover new drugs?
faq.answer: No. It helps triage molecules for review and experiments.

faq.question: Can it process large libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. The included workflow supports batch files and parallel processing when dependencies are installed.

faq.question: Does it require RDKit?
faq.answer: The underlying medchem ecosystem uses RDKit through Python chemistry libraries.

faq.question: Can I use custom property limits?
faq.answer: Yes. The script and API examples cover molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen bonds, and rotatable bonds.

faq.question: Are filtered compounds always bad?
faq.answer: No. Many valid drugs fail common filters, so results need expert review.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: The skill documentation links to project resources, but the included script works on local input files.
